findings.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:29 — The deleteMany's `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` OR-branch is not scoped by `method: SMS`, so any future/other code path (e.g. Email reminders) that increments the shared `retryCount` column would have its pending, still-needed reminders silently deleted by this SMS-only cron with no user-facing error.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:184 — retryCount is updated using a read-then-write pattern (reminder.retryCount + 1) based on a value fetched earlier in the request rather than an atomic Prisma increment, risking lost updates if the same reminder row is processed by an overlapping/concurrent cron invocation

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:184 — New retryCount increment on twilio.scheduleSMS() returning falsy (else branch) ships with no unit/integration test exercising that path.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:195 — New retryCount increment in the catch block for thrown scheduling exceptions has no test coverage verifying the reminder is updated rather than silently dropped.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:31 — New deleteMany OR clause (retryCount > 1) is untested, including the risk that it deletes non-SMS WorkflowReminder rows solely because retryCount happens to exceed 1, since the retryCount condition is not scoped with method: WorkflowMethods.SMS.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:56 — No regression test confirms the existing successful SMS-scheduling path still works after adding retryCount to the select clause and casting to the extended PartialWorkflowReminder type.

goldens.comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:184 — New retryCount increment on twilio.scheduleSMS() returning falsy (else branch) ships with no unit/integration test exercising that path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new else-branch that increments `retryCount` when `twilio.scheduleSMS()` returns a falsy value, but the claim that it "ships with no unit/integration test exercising that path" is not verifiable from this diff alone (tests could exist unchanged elsewhere). The diff shows no test additions/removals, but absence of test changes does not prove absence of coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:195 — New retryCount increment in the catch block for thrown scheduling exceptions has no test coverage verifying the reminder is updated rather than silently dropped.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add logic to increment `retryCount` in both the `else` branch and the `catch` block (around line ~195), but the finding’s claim that there is “no test coverage” cannot be verified from this diff alone. No test files are shown, and existing tests could already cover this behavior. The diff only proves new logic was added, not the absence of coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:31 — New deleteMany OR clause (retryCount > 1) is untested, including the risk that it deletes non-SMS WorkflowReminder rows solely because retryCount happens to exceed 1, since the retryCount condition is not scoped with method: WorkflowMethods.SMS.

adjudication.rationale: In scheduleSMSReminders.ts, the new deleteMany filter is `OR: [{ method: SMS, scheduledDate <= now }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]`. The `retryCount > 1` branch is not scoped by `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`, so it will delete any `WorkflowReminder` row (including non-SMS) whose retryCount exceeds 1. That’s a concrete, diff-verifiable risk of unintended data deletion introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:56 — No regression test confirms the existing successful SMS-scheduling path still works after adding retryCount to the select clause and casting to the extended PartialWorkflowReminder type.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the queried shape of `unscheduledReminders` by adding `retryCount` to the Prisma `select` and changing the cast to `(PartialWorkflowReminder & { retryCount: number })[]`, and later relies on `reminder.retryCount` when updating. No corresponding test changes are shown in this PR to exercise the existing “successful SMS scheduling” path with the new selected field/type expectation, so a reviewer could reasonably ask for a regression test around this modified data flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:1 — The PR introduces retry-count tracking behavior across three code paths but adds/modifies zero test files (no existing test suite covers this handler at all), so the behavioral change ships entirely untested.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new retryCount behavior in scheduleSMSReminders.ts (deleting reminders with retryCount > 1, selecting retryCount, incrementing it on failure paths, and a new DB column/migration), but the PR changes only application code and Prisma schema/migration with no accompanying test additions/updates shown in the diff. The claim that "no existing test suite covers this handler at all" cannot be verified from the diff alone, but it is verifiable that this nontrivial behavior change ships without any test changes in this PR.
